## Which tours through Ometepe are available?

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with a required visit to [Ometepe Island](/nicaragua/place/ometepe-island/). [“Best of Nicaragua: Volcanoes, Ometepe and the Pacific Ocean”](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/) is a **10-day, 9-night journey** through the country's historic cities, natural areas and Pacific coast.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_nicaragua_best_10_days}}

Ometepe is part of the main itinerary. That does not turn the entire tour into a multi-day island expedition. **One night** is allocated to Ometepe: the group arrives from the mainland and explores the island on day five, then returns by ferry and travels onward on day six.

The number of nights and the actual activities on the island are the first things worth checking. If you want several days for Ometepe's trails, beaches and villages, you will need a different, longer island program.

## Why Ometepe stands out among Nicaragua's destinations

The island lies in [Lake Nicaragua](/nicaragua/place/lake-nicaragua/), with its silhouette shaped by **Concepción** and **Maderas** volcanoes. Concepción remains active. Maderas is known for its forested slopes and variety of habitats. The two parts of Ometepe offer different scenery, and road travel between particular places can take a substantial part of the day.

Since 2010, Ometepe has belonged to UNESCO's World Network of **Biosphere Reserves** under the Man and the Biosphere Programme. This recognizes its natural and cultural significance; it should not be confused with UNESCO World Heritage status. The island has humid forests, coastal areas and archaeological traces of pre-Columbian cultures.

But Ometepe's geographic richness extends beyond any single tour. **Climbs of Concepción and Maderas, visits to all archaeological sites and detailed nature trails are not listed in this program.** Choose your journey by the paid excursions and daily itinerary, not merely by a general description of Ometepe as a destination.

The island's landscapes and attractions are described on the [Ometepe page](/nicaragua/place/ometepe-island/). Here, the focus is on choosing an existing tour and its logistics.

## Day five: San Jorge, the ferry and Ojo de Agua

After the sightseeing section in Granada, travelers head for the port of [San Jorge](/nicaragua/place/san-jorge/). They then take a **ferry across the lake** to Ometepe. Arrival time determines how much sightseeing is possible, so sailing times and onward transport are agreed when arranging the tour.

After the crossing, the program includes [Ojo de Agua](/nicaragua/place/ojo-de-agua/), natural pools fed by underground springs and surrounded by tropical trees. This is a peaceful stop beside the water, in contrast with the previous day's canopy activities at [Mombacho](/nicaragua/place/mombacho-volcano/).

The separate excursion module is [“Ometepe and Ojo de Agua with Ferry Crossing”](/nicaragua/ometepe-island/ometepe-ojo-de-agua-ferry/). It confirms that **the ferry itself and a visit to the springs are included**. However, swimming time, the exact island stop and additional services at the pools are not separately guaranteed.

Accommodation for the fifth night is on Ometepe. The program documents list both **Villa Colonial** and **Villa Paraiso**; the final hotel and overnight location are confirmed before booking. These should not be presented as two simultaneously included hotel stays.

## Day six: returning from the island and reaching the coast

The following day, travelers return to the ferry, cross [Lake Nicaragua](/nicaragua/place/lake-nicaragua/) and arrive at San Jorge. A **private overland transfer to San Juan del Sur** on the Pacific coast follows.

Day six is therefore **a travel day**, not another full day available to explore Ometepe. The program does not require a repeat visit to Mombacho, a climb of Ometepe's volcanoes or an extensive sightseeing program after disembarking.

Three free days then follow in [San Juan del Sur](/nicaragua/place/san-juan-del-sur/). This significantly changes the nature of the journey: the island visit is combined with relaxation by the ocean. Travelers who prefer active excursions every day should assess the length of the beach section; those seeking a varied single-country journey may find this sequence appealing.

## Comparing ways to visit Ometepe

| Format | What travelers get |
|---|---|
| One night | Ferry crossing and selected excursion |
| Several nights | More time in different areas |
| Volcano climb | Separate route and preparation |
| Countrywide tour | Ometepe together with other regions |

The **current 10-day itinerary** follows the final format with a single overnight stay. Ometepe fits between colonial Granada and the Pacific coast. There is time to experience the island and visit Ojo de Agua, but no promise of completing all its nature trails.

The right format depends on your aims. A short island stage within a larger tour works for seeing its landscapes, taking the ferry and enjoying the springs. Hiking the volcanoes, observing nature in different parts of the island and relaxing at an unhurried pace require a different distribution of time. A listing of [Ometepe in Nicaragua wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/nicaragua/) does not in itself confirm that every tour includes the same excursions.

## Transport, accommodation and included services

**The ferry must be planned as part of the itinerary, not an optional boat outing.** Strong winds, weather and changing ferry operations can affect the crossing. It would be inaccurate to fix next year's departure time from an old timetable. Our route goes from San Jorge to Ometepe and back, without promising a particular sailing hour.

The 10-day tour includes scheduled transport, excursions with an English-speaking guide, admission tickets to the listed attractions, nine nights of accommodation and meals on confirmed days. **Breakfast is specified for day five.** Personal expenses and extra activities are excluded from the base price.

Bring footwear for wet conditions, sun and rain protection, and swimwear if you plan to bathe. The presence of volcanoes in Nicaragua does not mean serious mountaineering equipment is necessary for this island stage: no such climb is included.

We offer **departures in 2027**, excluding Christmas, Easter and New Year periods, for groups of at least two. The exact accommodation and ferry logistics need confirmation when booking. The sequence of all days appears in the [complete Nicaragua tour](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/).

## Where to go after Ometepe

If the island interests you alongside the country's history and volcanic regions, consider the sequence connecting [Granada](/nicaragua/place/granada/), [Masaya Volcano](/nicaragua/place/masaya-volcano-national-park/) and [Mombacho](/nicaragua/place/mombacho-volcano/). They offer different natural experiences, although they lie within the same part of the extended route.

For a quieter island experience, Ometepe includes a stop at [Ojo de Agua](/nicaragua/place/ojo-de-agua/). After the island, the tour leads to the ocean in [San Juan del Sur](/nicaragua/place/san-juan-del-sur/). It is easier to compare these stages via [all Nicaragua tours](/nicaragua/tour/) than from an excursion title alone.

## Frequently asked questions about Ometepe tours

### How many nights are spent on Ometepe?

The current Ada Tours itinerary includes **one night**. The ferry crossing and Ojo de Agua visit are scheduled for day five; the return to the mainland is on day six.

### Is climbing Concepción or Maderas included?

No. The published island section lists a ferry crossing and Ojo de Agua. Volcano climbs require a separate itinerary with confirmed conditions and physical demands.

### How do travelers reach the island on this tour?

By overland transfer to [San Jorge](/nicaragua/place/san-jorge/), then ferry across Lake Nicaragua. The group takes the ferry again on the return journey before heading for the Pacific Ocean.

### Is the Ometepe day free time?

No. Day five involves an organized transfer, ferry crossing and spring visit. Free days are scheduled later in San Juan del Sur.

### Are Ojo de Agua and the island the same attraction?

No. [Ometepe](/nicaragua/place/ometepe-island/) is a large volcanic island; [Ojo de Agua](/nicaragua/place/ojo-de-agua/) is a separate attraction with natural pools on it. A visit to the springs is not a comprehensive visit to the entire island.

### Which conditions should be checked before travel?

The ferry crossings on days five and six, Ometepe accommodation, time at Ojo de Agua and swimming arrangements are particularly important. They are agreed with the full [10-day itinerary](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/).

## San Jorge: the port and ferry to Ometepe Island

[San Jorge](/nicaragua/place/san-jorge/) is a small town in the Rivas Department on the shore of [Lake Nicaragua](/nicaragua/place/lake-nicaragua/). For travelers, it is mainly associated with the crossing to [Ometepe](/nicaragua/place/ometepe-island/). Ferries and passenger boats depart from the harbor, offering views across the lake toward the island's volcanic peaks.

San Jorge can look like a brief transport stop, but its organization affects the whole journey. Arriving for the correct sailing, choosing the island port and allowing for wind and boarding time are much more important than trying to rush around town.

## How the lake crossing works

Ferries run from the San Jorge area to Ometepe's docks, including Moyogalpa and San José del Sur. These ports are in different parts of the island, so planning should account not only for time on the water but also for the distance from the arrival dock to your hotel or excursion.

Schedules may change, particularly because of weather or maintenance. Conditions for boarding with a vehicle or bulky luggage must be checked separately. Do not assume that every passenger sailing can carry vehicles.

Strong winds can raise waves on the lake. Travelers prone to motion sickness should consider the vessel type and expected conditions.

## What you can see from the ferry

On the crossing, the Concepción and Maderas volcanoes gradually rise into view, shaping the silhouette of [Ometepe Island](/nicaragua/place/ometepe-island/). This geography is already visible from San Jorge's shore, but from the ferry the peaks come closer and the shape of the coastline changes.

Lake Cocibolca is a major freshwater ecosystem connected with fishing and local transport. Protect cameras and other devices from spray and wind. Never approach unguarded parts of the deck or ignore crew directions to get a photograph.

## Combining San Jorge, Ometepe and Granada

San Jorge is close to the transport hub of Rivas, making it convenient for journeys between [Granada](/nicaragua/place/granada/), [Ometepe](/nicaragua/place/ometepe-island/) and the Pacific coast. These places offer contrasting experiences: Granada has architecture and [Las Isletas](/nicaragua/place/granada-islets/), Ometepe volcanic scenery, and San Jorge the crossing between mainland and island.

On our [10-day Ada Tours itinerary through Nicaragua](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/), day five crosses from San Jorge to Ometepe, followed by a visit to Ojo de Agua. The following day returns by ferry and continues to the Pacific coast. It shows how a port can become part of a well-connected itinerary.

## Practical advice

Arrive at the port with spare time, keeping documents and small change accessible. Confirm the vessel, actual timetable, baggage limits and arrival port. Weather can affect the crossing, so allow a reasonable margin before the next transfer.

A short stop in San Jorge is enough to see the shore and harbor. If you want more time for nature, it makes better sense to spend it on Ometepe than add arbitrary stops around the port.

## Frequently asked questions about San Jorge

### Where is San Jorge?

On the shore of Lake Nicaragua in the Rivas Department.

### Where do the ferries go?

To docks on [Ometepe Island](/nicaragua/place/ometepe-island/), including Moyogalpa and San José del Sur.

### Can I buy a ticket in advance?

Ticket sales depend on the carrier and vessel. Check the current arrangements for the specific sailing.

### Is San Jorge included on Ada Tours itineraries?

Yes, for example on the [10-day “Best of Nicaragua” tour](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/) with a ferry crossing to Ometepe.

## San Jorge on a Nicaragua itinerary: the ferry connecting lake and ocean

Travelers come to [San Jorge](/nicaragua/place/san-jorge/) primarily to cross [Lake Nicaragua](/nicaragua/place/lake-nicaragua/), also known as Cocibolca. This small port in Rivas Department is a departure point for ferries to [Ometepe Island](/nicaragua/place/ometepe-island/). As the ferry approaches, the Concepción and Maderas volcanoes come into view, forming the island's unmistakable silhouette.

The port connects two different parts of the journey. On one side are [Granada's](/nicaragua/place/granada/) old streets, volcanic slopes and lake islands. On the other lies [San Juan del Sur](/nicaragua/place/san-juan-del-sur/), with its Pacific bay and beaches. Between them is an island stop that cannot simply be replaced with an ordinary car excursion.

Our selection currently features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Every route in this selection passes through San Jorge as a main itinerary stop, not an optional excursion.

## Which days involve San Jorge?

On [“Best of Nicaragua: Volcanoes, Ometepe and the Pacific Ocean”](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/), the crossing is built into a 10-day, 9-night itinerary.

**Day 5.** After exploring Granada and Mombacho Volcano, travelers arrive at San Jorge, board the ferry and sail to Ometepe. Once on the island, they visit [Ojo de Agua](/nicaragua/place/ojo-de-agua/), natural pools with clear water. The night is spent on the island. Villa Colonial or Villa Paraiso are named as accommodation options; the final hotel is confirmed before booking.

**Day 6.** Travelers return from Ometepe to San Jorge by ferry. The overland section then begins: a private transfer from the port to San Juan del Sur on the Pacific. Here, San Jorge is where travelers change from ferry to car. The overnight stay is on the coast.

This arrangement provides an island stage between two transfers. Guests do not need to plan a separate journey to the island and back independently: both crossings are part of the main tour sequence.

## Comparing this option with other tours

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_nicaragua_best_10_days}}

The order of days is more useful than simply comparing attraction names. On this itinerary, [León](/nicaragua/place/leon/) and Granada come first, [Mombacho](/nicaragua/place/mombacho-volcano/) and the lake in the middle, and Pacific relaxation at the end. Three free days follow arrival in San Juan del Sur; optional activities on the coast are paid separately.

If you want several days entirely on Ometepe without a larger countrywide itinerary, this specific 10-day tour may be more intensive than you need. For those wishing to combine colonial towns, volcanoes, the lake and the ocean, the two visits through San Jorge allow the island to be included without dropping the other regions.

## What to consider before the ferry

**Arrival time at the port.** Ferry schedules and the exact dock must be confirmed for the chosen day. Sailings depend on the operator, weather and lake conditions; this article does not state a universal departure time.

**Luggage and transfers.** In San Jorge the form of transport changes. Keep island essentials handy: swimwear for Ojo de Agua, a hat and sun protection. How suitcases travel and how the car connects with the ferry are arranged under the specific tour conditions.

**The island day.** The day-five itinerary lists a ferry and [Ojo de Agua](/nicaragua/place/ojo-de-agua/), but not climbs of Ometepe's two volcanoes. This is an important distinction: the island is an introduction to nature and the lake, not a compulsory demanding trek.

**The following day.** After returning by ferry, guests travel to [San Juan del Sur](/nicaragua/place/san-juan-del-sur/). Arrival on the mainland is thus not the end of a sightseeing day but the beginning of a transfer to the ocean. A private transfer from the port is already included.

## What to see before and after San Jorge

Before the ferry, the route includes the [Granada Islets, Las Isletas](/nicaragua/place/granada-islets/) and a canopy experience near [Mombacho](/nicaragua/place/mombacho-volcano/). This is a different lake experience: the boat travels among small islets near Granada rather than crossing to the much larger Ometepe Island. The two boat journeys are easily confused when skimming a tour, although they take place on separate days and visit different areas.

After Ometepe, the journey turns to Pacific beaches. [San Juan del Sur](/nicaragua/place/san-juan-del-sur/) has time for independent relaxation. Surfing, sea outings and fishing are available activities in the region, but they are not automatically included in this tour's price.

For an overview of destinations, explore [Nicaragua tours](/nicaragua/tour/) and [nature journeys in Nicaragua](/interests/wildlife/tours/nicaragua/), if their programs match your interests. The [Nicaragua country page](/nicaragua/) describes the country and its regions.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is San Jorge a separate excursion or a stop en route?

On the current 10-day tour, it is a transport stop on the main route: the ferry to Ometepe begins and ends here. A stand-alone sightseeing excursion through San Jorge's streets is not part of the program.

### How many times do travelers pass through the port?

Twice. On day five, they leave for Ometepe; on day six, they return to San Jorge and continue to San Juan del Sur.

### Is an overnight stay in San Jorge required?

No overnight stay there is listed. After the first crossing, guests stay on Ometepe; after returning, they stay on the Pacific coast.

### Can you see Ometepe's volcanoes from the ferry?

Concepción and Maderas form the island's silhouette when seen from the lake. How clearly they appear depends on clouds and conditions on the water.

### Where can I confirm ferry times and inclusions?

Details of the departure, ferry and transfers are agreed for the [specific Nicaragua tour](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/). Do not rely on an unrelated independent ferry timetable or fare rather than the conditions of the booked program.

## San Juan del Sur: Pacific Ocean relaxation in Nicaragua

**San Juan del Sur** is a seaside town in Rivas Department in southwestern [Nicaragua](/nicaragua/). Its characteristic landscape is a broad bay, coastal hills, boats on the water and sunsets over the Pacific. It is a convenient place to spend a few days by the ocean after a busy route through cities and volcanoes.

The resort offers two distinctly different experiences: peaceful walks and relaxing beside the town bay, or outings to beaches with conditions suitable for surfing. Choose activities according to **the particular stretch of coast**, because open-ocean surf and a sheltered bay behave differently.

## The town bay and nearby beaches: what is the difference?

In the center of San Juan del Sur, you can walk along the seafront, watch fishing boats and spend the evening by the water. Half a day is enough for an independent introduction to town without a long transfer. Viewpoints on the surrounding hills overlook the curve of the bay.

For surfing, travelers generally head to nearby beaches. One of the best-known is **Playa Maderas**, north of town, surrounded by rocky shores and popular with surfers. Nicaragua's official tourism portal describes a journey of about 25 minutes from town, although actual travel time depends on road and transport conditions.

| Place | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Town bay | Walks and sunsets |
| Playa Maderas | Surfing and ocean waves |
| Playa Remanso | Beach day and surfing |
| Playa Hermosa | Nature and seaside relaxation |

Maderas, Remanso and Hermosa are all in the San Juan del Sur region, but are not within easy walking distance of each other. Choose one or two before the outing, accounting for actual transfers and swimming conditions.

## Surfing, fishing and coastal walks

Surfing depends on wave height and direction, wind, tides and the conditions at a particular beach. Suitable spots and timing can differ for beginners and experienced surfers. A nearby surf school does not mean lessons are already included in a purchased tour.

San Juan del Sur has a fishing tradition. Anyone interested in sea fishing should separately agree on the boat outing, seasonal restrictions, tackle and safety. **Visiting a fishing town does not automatically make a trip a fishing tour.**

Families and travelers who prefer a leisurely pace can alternate between beach time and town walks. But exposed ocean waters are not equally calm at every beach. Check swimming conditions on the same day.

To browse by travel interest, open [Nicaragua beach tours](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/nicaragua/) and compare the actual amount of time allocated to the coast.

## Connecting San Juan del Sur with Ometepe

A route through southwestern Nicaragua often combines volcanic scenery with the Pacific. [Ometepe Island](/nicaragua/place/ometepe-island/) lies in [Lake Nicaragua](/nicaragua/place/lake-nicaragua/), so travelers need a water crossing back to the mainland before reaching the coastal resort.

One important transport point is [San Jorge](/nicaragua/place/san-jorge/). From there, the route continues overland to San Juan del Sur. Allow time for the ferry timetable, the road transfer and hotel check-in. The transfer day is best not overloaded with independent ocean activities.

## What is actually included in the Ada Tours itinerary?

On the current [10-day “Best of Nicaragua” itinerary](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/), travelers arrive in San Juan del Sur on **day six** after visiting Ometepe. **Days seven to nine** are free for relaxation and exploring the town and surroundings independently. **Day ten** includes a transfer to Managua Airport.

This is a significant feature of the program: travelers have several consecutive days by the ocean and choose how to spend them. **Surf lessons, fishing and additional boat trips are not listed as included activities**; their details and cost are agreed separately. Accommodation and meal arrangements during the free days are confirmed before booking under the specific tour terms.

For travelers chiefly interested in volcanoes, cities and the lake, this itinerary preserves the main sightseeing section before the coast. If your priority is the ocean and surfing, compare the free days with the number of activities you would like, without assuming all marine experiences have already been paid for.

## When to go and how to choose beach days

On Nicaragua's Pacific side, the generally drier period is approximately **November to April**, and the rainy period approximately **May to October**. For surfing and swimming, however, the calendar is only a guide. Wave height, wind, road conditions and local advice matter more on a particular day.

For the coast, bring light clothes, a hat, sunscreen and comfortable walking shoes. If you plan to visit other beaches or take a boat, confirm transport and rescheduling arrangements in case of bad weather.

When combining a beach holiday with sightseeing around the country, consult the [Nicaragua tour catalog](/nicaragua/tour/) and check exactly how many free days each itinerary offers, rather than simply counting nights in a seaside town.

## Frequently asked questions about San Juan del Sur

### Is San Juan del Sur on the Caribbean Sea?

No. The town is on the **Pacific Ocean**. For Caribbean beaches and reefs, explore other destinations such as the [Corn Islands](/nicaragua/place/corn-islands/).

### Can I surf directly in the town bay?

Surfing generally takes place at neighboring open-ocean beaches, particularly Playa Maderas. Suitable waves and safety depend on conditions and the participant's skill level.

### How many free days are there on the current 10-day tour?

On “Best of Nicaragua,” there are **three free days, days seven through nine**, after arriving on the coast on day six.

### Is fishing included in the beach days?

There is no confirmation that fishing is included in this itinerary. It is a separate activity to be arranged on request.

## Tours through San Juan del Sur: ocean relaxation after Nicaragua's volcanoes

[San Juan del Sur](/nicaragua/place/san-juan-del-sur/) lies in Rivas Department on Nicaragua's Pacific coast. The town stands beside a horseshoe-shaped bay. The center has a beach, cafés and places to walk, while nearby stretches of coast are popular for surfing or more secluded relaxation. The hills offer views over town and ocean.

San Juan del Sur is a convenient final stop on a multi-city itinerary: after the intensive sightseeing section, travelers can choose each day's activities themselves. That is the structure of the current Ada Tours program visiting this resort. Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}.

A detailed introduction to the town, beaches and attractions appears on the [San Juan del Sur page](/nicaragua/place/san-juan-del-sur/). Here, you can compare specific tours and see how the coastal section fits into each journey.

## How San Juan del Sur fits the 10-day tour

[“Best of Nicaragua: Volcanoes, Ometepe and the Pacific Ocean”](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/) lasts 10 days and nine nights. It starts in Managua, passes through [León](/nicaragua/place/leon/), [Granada](/nicaragua/place/granada/), the [Masaya Volcano region](/nicaragua/place/masaya-volcano-national-park/) and [Mombacho](/nicaragua/place/mombacho-volcano/), then continues to [Ometepe Island](/nicaragua/place/ometepe-island/).

**Day six.** After staying overnight on Ometepe, travelers return by ferry across the lake to [San Jorge port](/nicaragua/place/san-jorge/). From there, a private transfer leads directly to San Juan del Sur. Victoriano or Alcazar is listed as the accommodation option; the final hotel is confirmed before booking.

**Days seven to nine.** Three free days for relaxing by the Pacific, walks and independent exploration of the town. The accommodation table lists Alcazar for these nights. Meal arrangements for the free days and the final hotel are agreed when booking.

**Day ten.** After breakfast, a transfer takes travelers from San Juan del Sur to Augusto C. Sandino International Airport in Managua.

This is a main stop on the route, not an optional outing. If you are choosing the tour for time beside the sea, days seven to nine are important: they are free of obligatory multi-hour excursions.

## Available tours and what to compare

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_nicaragua_best_10_days}}

The current itinerary combines travel around the country with time on one coast. Its opening days focus on colonial-town culture, volcanic scenery and [Lake Nicaragua](/nicaragua/place/lake-nicaragua/). Ocean relaxation follows. This works for travelers seeking variety without having to change destinations every day at the end of their holiday.

Inclusions apply to the full tour: scheduled transport, specified excursions, admission tickets, an English-speaking guide during the sightseeing section, accommodation and meals as confirmed in the program. Extra activities on free days cost more. **Free time on the coast does not mean that surfing, sea fishing or boat outings are already included in the price.**

For itineraries with other priorities, browse [all Nicaragua tours](/nicaragua/tour/) or [Nicaragua beach tours](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/nicaragua/). These catalogs display current programs, but each tour's exact included services must still be checked.

## What to do on the coast during free days

In San Juan del Sur, you can spend time around the central bay, walk beside the water, choose cafés and watch the sunset. A well-known viewpoint with a statue of Christ of Mercy rises above town. On nearby beaches, including Maderas and Hermosa, surfing is popular; wave size and suitability vary by beach, date and the traveler's experience.

Boat outings and fishing are also offered in the area. These are possibilities at the destination, not a list of Ada Tours services already booked. To turn a free day into a guided activity or water excursion, arrange the operator, transport, price and participant requirements separately.

Those preferring a slower holiday can enjoy the central bay and town walks. Families and novice surfers should distinguish the sheltered bay from nearby beaches with stronger surf: one wave forecast cannot be applied to the entire coastline.

## When to plan the beach section

Seasonal conditions on Nicaragua's Pacific coast are noticeable. In the drier months, longer outdoor walks are generally easier to plan, while the rainy season makes the scenery greener and weather can change during the day. Weather does not follow a rigid calendar, however, and surf conditions depend on the particular beach.

Departure dates for this tour are agreed separately. If you plan surfing, a boat outing or sport fishing, identify the priority activity first, then check dates, sea conditions and local operators' schedules. That way, free days need not be spent waiting for an excursion that was never confirmed.

The sightseeing part of the journey also includes nature activities: a private boat trip among the [Granada Islets](/nicaragua/place/granada-islets/) and a canopy experience at [Mombacho](/nicaragua/place/mombacho-volcano/). Do not confuse these with possible Pacific coast activities: the places and days are different.

## Who will enjoy this end to the itinerary?

**Travelers who want to see a lot of Nicaragua in one journey.** Before beach relaxation, the route covers colonial towns, Masaya Volcano National Park, the lake, a ferry to Ometepe and the natural springs at [Ojo de Agua](/nicaragua/place/ojo-de-agua/).

**Travelers who want genuine free days.** Three consecutive days can be devoted to the beach, walks or activities you choose independently. Confirm meals and accommodation for this section in advance.

**Travelers expecting a fully organized surf camp.** This itinerary does not advertise that format. It offers time beside the coast, while lessons, equipment, extra outings and other local services require separate arrangements.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many days does the tour spend in San Juan del Sur?

Arrival is scheduled on day six, followed by three free days, from day seven through day nine. On day ten, travelers leave for Managua Airport.

### Are surfing lessons and sea fishing included?

No. These activities are not listed among the confirmed inclusions of this tour. Extra activities during free days cost more and are arranged on request.

### How do travelers reach San Juan del Sur from Ometepe?

First by ferry across the lake to San Jorge, then by private road transfer from the port to the Pacific coast. Both stages belong to day six.

### Can I replace a free day with an excursion?

You can choose extra activities at the resort, but the specific option needs separate agreement. The presence of three free days does not mean an additional excursion is included.

### Where does the journey finish?

Day ten features a transfer from San Juan del Sur to Managua International Airport. The departure time is arranged around the flight and actual road conditions.

### Are there tours devoted solely to beach relaxation?

This page shows routes that **necessarily visit San Juan del Sur**. For a wider selection, including trips with a different balance of sightseeing and relaxation, use the [Nicaragua beach tours selection](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/nicaragua/).
